discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a new Z2 invariant, with helical edge states protected by time-reversal symmetry. This was the first topological phase outside the quantum Hall regime, and it led directly to three-dimensional topological insulators. In 2007 Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental proof. In HgTe/CdTe quantum wells they observed quantized edge conductance of about 2e^2/h that appeared only above the critical well thickness, and later nonlocal measurements confirmed helical edge transport. Together these works founded the field of symmetry-protected topological matter. They opened the way to topological superconductivity, Majorana and higher-order topological states, and new spintronic and quantum-information concepts. This is a clear case where a clean theoretical idea was turned into an unambiguous experimental discovery that has reshaped condensed matter physics.
